function_question: How does nature build strong things from very little material?

opening.text: There was a boy called Ravi in Room 3 who loved the little class library in the corner.
At reading time, Ravi picked a new book from the shelf and curled up with a story.
The shelf sagged in the middle and tipped every book onto the floor, again! There was no money for a new one, just a big pile of scrap paper and cardboard.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Room 3's shelf keeps dumping books on the floor, and all Ravi has is scrap paper. Can you help him build a new one? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature solved this millions of years ago. Tap each card to meet four nature heroes who build strong and light!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which paper column will hold the most books?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your shelf like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your shelf and let's see how many books it holds for each sheet of paper!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Room 3's books sit safely on YOUR paper shelf, and other classes keep asking how to build one too!

quick_check.question: Ravi's shelf holds 12 books and uses 4 sheets of paper. How many books per sheet is that?
quick_check.right: Right! 12 ÷ 4 = 3 books per sheet. A higher score means a stronger shelf from less paper.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Share 12 books equally between 4 sheets.

clue_cards.name: Honeybees
clue_cards.trick: Six-sided wax cells that fit together with no gaps.
clue_cards.does: They hold the most honey for the least wax, and each wall supports its neighbours.

clue_cards.name: Bird bones
clue_cards.trick: Hollow inside, with thin cross-braces like tiny trusses.
clue_cards.does: Light enough to fly, but strong enough to land.

clue_cards.name: Bamboo
clue_cards.trick: A hollow tube divided by solid walls called nodes.
clue_cards.does: The nodes stop it buckling, so bamboo can grow 30 m tall.

clue_cards.name: Giant water lily
clue_cards.trick: A huge leaf braced underneath by a web of ribs.
clue_cards.does: It can hold a small child, and it inspired the roof of the Crystal Palace in London.

predict.prompt: Bends or holds? Put a book on each sheet of paper. Predict first!
predict.explain: Same paper, different shape. Tubes and hexagons spread the load across many walls, so they hold much more than a flat sheet.

lab.title: The paper column lab
lab.predict: Which paper column will hold the most books?

tool.name: SCAMPER
tool.intro: SCAMPER is a set of magic question words. Each letter is a different way to change an idea. Today you'll use all 7 letters in one go!

parts.name: Substitute
parts.example: 🪑 Swap wooden legs for card tubes.
parts.starter: Instead of a wooden plank, the shelf could be…

parts.name: Combine
parts.example: 🪑 Chair + box = a seat with storage.
parts.starter: I could combine tubes and hexagons by…

parts.name: Adapt
parts.what: Borrow an idea from somewhere else.
parts.example: 🪑 Hollow legs, like a bird bone.
parts.starter: I could adapt bamboo's nodes by…

parts.name: Modify
parts.example: 🪑 Make the legs wider at the bottom.
parts.starter: To make it stronger, I could change the shape of…

parts.name: Put to another use
parts.example: 🪑 Use it as a little table.

parts.name: Eliminate
parts.example: 🪑 No back: now it's a stool.
parts.starter: I could save paper by leaving out…

parts.name: Reverse
parts.what: Flip it or turn it around.
parts.example: 🪑 Upside down, it's a doll's playpen.
parts.starter: What if the ribs went on top instead of…
